IMAPP is an Erasmus Mundus master in applied physics delivered by a European consortium with strong laboratory and instrumentation components. Its dedicated 2027-2028 timeline page lists the application windows, scholarship milestones and results dates for the next intake.

Programme Highlights

  • Applied-physics curriculum with instrumentation and materials focus
  • Dedicated 2027-2028 timeline page with all key dates
  • European mobility with research-lab placements
  • Doctoral progression and R&D employment for graduates

Who Should Apply

Physics and engineering-physics graduates with laboratory experience fit the programme; motivation and research interests carry weight in selection.

Funding and Costs

Erasmus Mundus scholarships for selected students per the published timeline.

Deadline and How to Apply

Open the IMAPP timeline page, note the window dates, and submit through the consortium's application system. Key deadline information: The 2027-2028 application timeline is published on the official timeline page.

Official Source

  • Official application page (verified link)

About IMAPP Consortium

The IMAPP consortium delivers the Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Applied Physics with European universities and research institutes.

Official website: https://imapp.eu

Contact

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be raised through the contact channel given on the official announcement page (see the Official Link section above). Always quote the position reference in your message so the admissions or HR team can route your enquiry quickly.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: See official page for dates - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.
